description: MSBuild's static graph with asm projects (the owner's choice of 2026-11-26: support -graph -isolate). With -isolate, a project may call only the project instances the graph predicted from ProjectReference items, with the targets ProjectReferenceTargets declared (MSB4252 otherwise; 0.4.0 failed at the C# app's first call into the asm library and at the program's first call into its static library). Restore first: NuGet's restore fails -isolate for any project, C# alone included. A C# app with an asm library, an asm program with two RIDs and the static libraries it links (one of them for both target frameworks), and a second program that links a static library which links another (a transitive reference): build, rebuild, clean, -o, and publish of the program and of the app for this machine's RID, each with -isolate.

steps.description: Restore apart from the graph build, which runs with --no-restore.

The whole solution: the app's calls into Lib (GetAsmConsumerInfo, GetAsmApiFile, GetAsmNativeRuntimeAssets) and each of Prog's RID builds' calls into Shared and Multi for that RID were predicted by the graph.
The app finds its library and calls it through the bindings the graph build wrote.

A rebuild: the common targets declare GetTargetFrameworks for Build and Clean but not for Rebuild, so .NET's own rebuild fails -isolate (a C# app and library alone, measured with SDK 11.0.100); the SDK declares it for the projects that use it.
Clean asks each asm reference for GetAsmConsumerInfo too.
The app alone: Lib is only a reference here, built for the app as its consumer targets ask.

-o: one folder per RID, and nothing else. The references build into their own bin/ in a graph build (a RID build's folders would make each RID's view of a reference an instance of its own, and the graph's transitive edges built that instance's RID builds a second time, into folders such as linux-x64/win-x64/).

A program whose static library links another: Shared reaches ChainProg only as a transitive reference, which the .NET SDK adds while the build runs, so the evaluation never prepared it; the SDK gives it the RID and the removals then (else, under -o, it was called with the RID build's OutputPath, an instance the graph never built: MSB4252, measured with SDK 11.0.100; SDK 10.0.101's assets file lists even direct references as transitive ones, which failed step 8 the same way). The link needs Shared's mul_ints.

A publish: asm projects declare the Publish protocol themselves (C# gets it from Microsoft.Managed.After.targets, which they do not import), and each RID build is published. No reference is built in a publish context of its own (no ASM0013 for the static libraries, no publish folder of theirs).
A RID-specific publish restores for that RID first.
The app for this machine's RID, its library next to it. The consumer calls GetAsmConsumerInfo without the RID, an instance the graph gets from a graph-only twin of the reference.
